original_question: What can be said in general about the number of distinct monomials appearing in the Schur function s_lambda(x_1, ..., x_n) for an arbitrary partition lambda?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Problem 25 ([Stan1999, Ch. 7 Exer. 33(c)]): "Can anything be said in general about the number of distinct monomials in the Schur function s_lambda(x1, . . . , xn) for arbitrary lambda?"
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's exact target almost verbatim: it asks about Schur functions/polynomials, the count of distinct monomials, and arbitrary partitions lambda, without drifting to broader neighboring problems.
missing_details: The quantifiers should be explicit: fix an integer n >= 1 and a partition lambda; because the expression is in n variables, one should either assume ell(lambda) <= n or state the usual convention that s_lambda(x1,...,xn)=0 when ell(lambda) > n.
The ambient ring should be identified, e.g. s_lambda(x1,...,xn) as an element of Z[x1,...,xn].
The phrase "number of distinct monomials" should be formalized as the cardinality of the support {alpha in N^n : the coefficient of x1^alpha1...xn^alphan in s_lambda(x1,...,xn) is nonzero}.
It should be explicit that monomials are counted without multiplicity; only nonzero occurrence matters, not the coefficient value.
The notation for partitions is implicit: lambda is a partition, ell(lambda) denotes its length, and when ell(lambda) <= n the Schur polynomial is homogeneous of degree |lambda|.

The paper's formulation is deliberately open-ended ("what can be said in general"), so a stand-alone rewrite should preserve that scope rather than force an exact formula, asymptotic regime, or classification not stated in the paper.
There are no operator definitions, nilpotency conditions, or "for all sufficiently large m" clauses attached to this target problem; those notions are inapplicable here.
refined_question: For each integer n >= 1 and each partition lambda, let s_lambda(x1, ..., xn) denote the Schur polynomial in Z[x1, ..., xn] (with the usual convention that s_lambda(x1, ..., xn)=0 if ell(lambda) > n). What can be said in general about the size of its monomial support, namely the cardinality of {alpha in N^n : [x1^alpha1 ... xn^alphan] s_lambda(x1, ..., xn) != 0}, i.e. the number of distinct monomials that occur with nonzero coefficient in s_lambda(x1, ..., xn)?
